claim.markdown_says:
Bopomofo:
312D-312F, 31B8-31BF Brahmi:   (specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 49030) ... then page-1214 opens with the bare line '11000-11046, 11066-1106F, 1107F' with no label
claim.why_it_matters: The 'Brahmi:' script label from the top of PDF page 1184 has been concatenated onto the end of the Bopomofo range line on the previous page. Two entries are corrupted at once: Bopomofo's range line now reads '31B8-31BF Brahmi:', and Brahmi's code-point ranges are left orphaned at the head of the next page with no label. This is the E.3.3 item 5 list of characters newly permitted in user-defined words - the script-to-range mapping is the data an implementer reads here, and it is broken at this boundary.

verdict.reasoning: Independently confirmed against 300dpi renders of both pages. PDF page 1213 (printed folio 1183) ends its body text with exactly two lines - 'Bopomofo:' then '312D-312F, 31B8-31BF' - followed by roughly a quarter page of whitespace and then the footer '(c)ISO/IEC 2023  1183'. I cropped the bottom band (y 2650-3050 of 3300) at full resolution and read the glyphs directly: there is no 'Brahmi:' token anywhere on page 1213. PDF page 1214 (printed folio 1184) opens, after the 'ISO/IEC 1989:2023 (E)' running head, with 'Brahmi:' on its own line followed by '11000-11046, 11066-1106F, 1107F', then 'Buginese:' / '1A00-1A1B'. The markdown does not match: specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 49029-49030 reads 'Bopomofo:' / '312D-312F, 31B8-31BF Brahmi:', and the page-1214 body (line 49036) begins with the bare, unlabelled line '11000-11046, 11066-1106F, 1107F'. Both halves of the claim's quotations are verbatim accurate. This is not page-break furniture, not reflow, and not a wrapping artifact: a semantic label has migrated across a page boundary onto a different entry's data line, so one entry's value line acquires foreign text and another entry loses its key entirely. Any reader or extractor consuming this script-to-range table gets a wrong Bopomofo line and a keyless Brahmi range set. The defect is also systematic rather than isolated - the identical failure recurs at the very next boundary, where markdown line 49094 (page-1214) ends the Cyrillic ranges with 'A67F-A69F, FE2E-FE2F Deseret:' although the PDF page 1214 body genuinely ends at 'A67F-A69F,' and 'FE2E-FE2F' plus the 'Deseret:' label belong to page 1215 - which corroborates that the transcription pipeline mis-joins the head of each following page onto the tail of the preceding one in this list.
verdict.corrected_description: Claim confirmed as described; no correction needed. Precise coordinates for the fix: PDF page 1213 = printed folio 1183, PDF page 1214 = printed folio 1184. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 49030 must be '312D-312F, 31B8-31BF' (drop the trailing ' Brahmi:'), and a 'Brahmi:' label line must be inserted immediately before line 49036 ('11000-11046, 11066-1106F, 1107F') at the head of the page-1214 body, matching the PDF's two-line label/ranges pattern used by every other entry in E.3.3 item 5. Note for the fixer: the same page-boundary join defect recurs at the 1214/1215 boundary (markdown line 49094, 'FE2E-FE2F Deseret:'), so this boundary should be repaired as part of a sweep of the whole Annex E script table rather than as a one-off edit.
